answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of gating it: each new agent must post a bond that an attestation graph can slash, so a sybil cluster only breaks even while its vouchers hold. Sampling a random vertex from that graph every epoch forces attackers to sustain honest-looking links on a whole ledge of the network rather than a chosen corner. When a cluster is flagged, its members' scores merge behind one lantern-like fingerprint, so N fake identities pay N bonds and lose them together. Cost scales with squared cluster size, which is the one thing a farmer cannot subsidise.
